Preserve Nisshin as the physical manufacturer and Aria/Greco as marketed identities for the supported pre-Maxon family; do not back-project that proof automatically onto every 1960s wedge fuzz.

Tone Machines Blog argues the Greco No.35, Sekova wedge fuzzes and Shaftesbury-type wedges belong to a common Japanese OEM family, with at least four enclosure/power variants and an earliest likely date around 1967. The physical factory remains unresolved and should not be inferred from family resemblance alone.

Preserve Lafayette as the marketed/distribution identity and keep the physical factory unresolved.

Melos is repeatedly associated with the LRE Fuzz Sound and later Univox-related Japanese effects. Current research specifically proposes Melos may have been the house brand of the otherwise unidentified manufacturer behind LRE/Uni-Wah/U-1095. Record this as a lead only; the existence of a Melos house-brand relationship does not establish Melos as the factory or as a standalone manufacturer.
